nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Little light reaches the floor under a closed beech canopy, so the forest floor is shaded for much of the growing season.

nodes.name: Cool, wet mountain climate
nodes.desc: Rain and snow on the Carpathian slopes keep the beech and fir forest moist.

nodes.name: Standing and fallen deadwood
nodes.desc: In unmanaged old forest, dead trees are left to stand and rot. They house beetles, fungi and the birds that feed on them.

nodes.name: Forest soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients released from rotting wood and leaf litter feed the trees and shrubs.

nodes.name: European beech
nodes.desc: The dominant tree of the site. UNESCO says beech has spread across Europe since the last Ice Age, and these stands show that natural process.

nodes.name: Silver fir
nodes.desc: A conifer that grows with beech in the mixed beech-fir stands that cover much of the Poloniny uplands.

nodes.name: Bilberry
nodes.desc: A low shrub of forest clearings and slopes whose berries are a summer food for bears and other animals.

nodes.name: Meadow grasses and herbs
nodes.desc: Grasses and flowers of glades and mountain meadows, grazed by deer and bison.

nodes.name: Yellow-necked mouse
nodes.desc: A forest rodent that eats seeds and is a main prey of wildcats in the Carpathians.

nodes.name: Bank vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent of woodland floors eating seeds, berries and green plants; prey of wildcats and adders.

nodes.name: Rosalia longicorn
nodes.desc: A blue-grey beetle whose larvae develop in dead and dying beech wood, so it depends on old forest.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots through the forest floor, eating roots, fallen seeds and invertebrates.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: A small forest deer that browses shrubs and herbs. Wikipedia says lynx prefer it as prey where it is common.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: A large grazer and browser of forest glades and meadows, and prey for wolves and lynx.

nodes.name: European bison
nodes.desc: Reintroduced to Poloniny National Park in 2004. It grazes grasses and browses woody plants.

nodes.name: White-backed woodpecker
nodes.desc: Eats mostly wood-boring beetles and larvae. It needs mature broadleaf forest with plenty of standing and fallen dead wood.

nodes.name: European wildcat
nodes.desc: A shy forest cat. In the Carpathians it feeds mainly on yellow-necked mice and voles.

nodes.name: Common adder
nodes.desc: A venomous snake of forest edges that eats small mammals, lizards and amphibians.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: Mostly plant-eating, taking berries, plants and mushrooms, plus insects, carrion and sometimes young or weak ungulates.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: A pack hunter of deer and wild boar, found across the Carpathian forests.

nodes.name: Eurasian lynx
nodes.desc: A solitary forest cat that hunts mainly deer, preferring roe deer where they are common.

nodes.name: Deadwood fungi
nodes.desc: Bracket fungi such as tinder fungus rot dead beech wood, returning nutrients and making wood softer for beetles.
